doc.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021

title: Building BEATBoxSAX and the first viral video
summary: Inspired by McFerrin he added percussion sounds to the saxophone, posted Catch'em Up to 100,000 views, and learned not to chase numbers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: amazing stuff you’ve ever heard, and the most creative stuff, and just being like I want to be able to do that but on the saxophone. And so then slowly over the years progressing and adding — oh wonder if I could get — I had this pop sound, I wonder if I could kind of get a hi-hat sound, and then thinking, also thinking of other instruments I’ve explored. I’ve played drumset a little bit and thinking okay so where’s my bass drum sound? Where’s my snare? Okay could I do like a roll sound? And then okay I have a bass could I do a mel — and all of it slowly came together soon enough, it was like oh I have a song here, I’ll post this online, let’s see what happens. And this video that I posted, I don’t know if it was like seven years ago, I called it Catch’em Up is the name of this composition that I wrote. And yes by then I had kind of thought of a name, BEATBoxSAX, just thinking like it kind of sound like beatboxing I guess, even though I don’t actually, I’ve never practiced vocally beatboxing. And that video did really well, surprisingly well. Like it got up to 100,000 views in a couple of weeks. And I was just like what? Oh my gosh. Wow. Okay. I was a little, once again kind of a little addicted to the applause so to speak. And then it’s funny because then right from then it was like, oh I need to do more, and I’ll do a cover song of a pop tune. And I remember even getting into the whole game here, and that is what you have to be careful with these days as a musician is thinking okay my first video got this number of views, this next video is going to be even better, it’s going to be a cover song, how could I do the angle, what’s going to be the best way to get more — okay “Every Breath You Take” by the Police, here we go. I put it out, it does like half as well. And I’m like depressed. It still got 50,000 views which, a month ago I would have been amazed but it doesn’t matter. So much in life is comparative. You know? We’re just comparing. And it’s just like only 50,000, and I was depressed. And from that point on I learned it’s not about the numbers. Yes I want my music to communicate. I want to reach people. But I’m not going to obsess over everything of like oh what’s going to get the best look? What’s going to get the most views? It’s got to be fun for me first and foremost. And then it’s icing on the cake if it connects — well more than icing on the cake but it’s just like that’s the sweet spot. If it’s something I truly love and it’s resonating with people, that is the sweet spot. That’s what I want to be doing.
